extracted.intended_audience: NeurIPS/ NIPS paper reviewers (program committee and external reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluation criteria for reviewing submissions to the NeurIPS (NIPS) conference, including required scores, qualitative criteria, procedural requirements (confidentiality, conflicts, double-blind), and expectations for review content and tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer load and review quality expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: We have reduced your load to a maximum of 5 (exceptionally 6) papers: please write detailed thoughtful reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write detailed, thoughtful reviews; short superficial reviews that venture uninformed opinions are worse than no review. Include pros and cons in your review. Anonymous reviews of accepted papers will be made public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: By viewing the papers, you agree that the NIPS review process is confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use ideas and results from submitted papers in your work, research or grant proposals until they appear in public formats. Do not distribute submitted papers or their ideas to anyone unless approved by the program chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing policy and reviewer conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers do not know the identity of the authors (area chairs do). Double blind is not perfect; reviewers may discover or think they have discovered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not actively attempt to discover author identities. If you suspect you've discovered an identity, first completely read the paper and then explain how and why in the 'Confidential comments to PC members' box to help the committee assess novelty and the effectiveness of double-blind reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit up to 10 MB of supplementary material (proofs, audio, images, video, data, source code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your responsibility is to read and judge the main paper; reading the supplement is optional. Before criticizing missing rigorous proofs or limited qualitative results, consider checking the supplementary material. Supplements may be pdf or archives (gz, tgz, zip, tar).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting, length and anonymity checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that papers follow submission guidelines for length (at most 9 pages; ninth page must contain only references), format, and anonymity, and that they are not jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify the program chairs immediately (program-chairs@nips.cc) if you find serious formatting issues or anonymity problems with a submitted paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection and reporting of previously published work / dual-submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where possible, identify submissions very similar or identical to previously published versions or concurrently submitted to other conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you detect violations of the dual submission policy, note this in the 'Confidential comments to PC members' section of the review form. See Author and Submission Instructions for clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary review purpose and framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on whether the paper adds value to the NIPS community and on the paper's quality as a scientific contribution rather than your personal interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer solid, technical papers that explore new territory or point out new directions rather than incremental advances. Summarize main ideas and relate them to previous work; discuss strengths and weaknesses and address Qualitative Evaluation criteria. Include a list of arguments pro and con acceptance. If out of scope, corroborate by checking the call for papers topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of review (short 1-2 sentence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fill in a 'Summary of review' — a short 1-2 sentence summary of your review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This summary should concisely capture your overall judgment for authors and program committee members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and specificity of reviewer comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer comments should be detailed, specific and polite, avoiding vague complaints and providing appropriate citations if authors are unaware of relevant work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even negative reviews can be polite and constructive. Do not write blunt, unhelpful one-line judgments. Think of the types of reviews you like to receive and provide actionable feedback to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments to PC members
rubrics_metrics.description: A box is provided for comments visible only to program committee members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this for oral vs poster recommendations, explicit comparisons to other submissions, disclosure of conflicts of interest discovered late, or more blunt criticisms you don't want sent to authors. If you suspect author identity or dual submissions, explain there.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative Quality Score (1-10) and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers give a quality score between 1 and 10 for each paper. The program committee interprets the numerical score as follows:
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
10: Top 5% of accepted NIPS papers, a seminal paper for the ages. I will consider not reviewing for NIPS again if this is rejected.
9: Top 15% of accepted NIPS papers, an excellent paper, a strong accept. I will fight for acceptance.
8: Top 50% of accepted NIPS papers, a very good paper, a clear accept. I vote and argue for acceptance.
7: Good paper, accept. I vote for acceptance, although would not be upset if it were rejected.
6: Marginally above the acceptance threshold. I tend to vote for accepting it, but leaving it out of the program would be no great loss.
5: Marginally below the acceptance threshold. I tend to vote for rejecting it, but having it in the program would not be that bad.
4: An OK paper, but not good enough. A rejection. I vote for rejecting it, although would not be upset if it were accepted.
3: A clear rejection. I vote and argue for rejection.
2: A strong rejection. I'm surprised it was submitted to this conference. I will fight for rejection.
1: Trivial or wrong or known. I'm surprised anybody wrote such a paper. I will consider not reviewing for NIPS again if this is accepted.
Scores should reflect absolute judgments of the contributions; do not adjust to achieve a desired distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact Score (2/1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Independently of the Quality Score, give an Impact Score to identify papers that are different, original, or potentially impactful for the NIPS community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
2: Work is different enough from typical submissions to potentially have a major impact on a subset of the NIPS community.
1: Work is incremental and unlikely to have much impact even if technically correct and well executed.
Use this to sort papers where other measures are less informative; quality and impact can disagree (e.g., technically strong but unlikely to generate follow-up research).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence Score (1-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers give a confidence score between 1 and 5 for each paper, interpreted as follows:
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
5: Absolutely certain evaluation is correct and very familiar with the literature.
4: Confident but not absolutely certain; unlikely but conceivable that reviewer missed something.
3: Fairly confident; possible reviewer did not understand certain parts or missed literature; mathematics/details not carefully checked.
2: Willing to defend the evaluation, but quite likely reviewer did not understand central parts.
1: Educated guess; either paper not in reviewer's area or extremely difficult to understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative Evaluation — Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper technically sound? Are claims well-supported by theoretical analysis or experimental results? Is this a complete piece of work, or merely a position paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the authors are careful and honest about evaluating both strengths and weaknesses. Comment on technical soundness and evidence supporting claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative Evaluation — Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper clearly written and well-organized? Does it adequately inform the reader?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A superbly written paper provides enough information for the expert reader to reproduce its results. If not clear, provide suggestions to improve the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative Evaluation — Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the problems or approaches new? Is this a novel combination of familiar techniques? Is it clear how this work differs from previous contributions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that related work is adequately referenced. Recommend checking recent NIPS proceedings to ensure the paper is significantly different from prior NIPS work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative Evaluation — Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the results important? Are others likely to use these ideas or build on them? Does the paper address a difficult problem in a better way than previous research?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the paper advances the state of the art in a demonstrable way, or provides unique data, conclusions, or theoretical/pragmatic approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author rebuttal and reviewer update process
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors have an opportunity to submit feedback on their reviews during the rebuttal period (Aug 4 - Aug 11).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read each rebuttal carefully and keep an open mind. If authors' comments change your assessment, update your review to explain why. Between Aug 11 and Aug 18 area chairs will lead discussions to reach consensus when necessary; engage in discussion and consider other reviewers' points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark conflicts of interest in the reviewing system for anyone who is or was recently your student or mentor, a current or recent colleague, or a close collaborator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in doubt, mark a conflict to avoid appearance of impropriety. Your own username should be auto-marked; if you have multiple accounts, mark them. If you do not mark a conflict, it is assumed you do not have one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject areas, paper matching and bidding
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter your subject areas into CMT and upload representative papers to the Toronto Paper Matching System to assist assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers were asked to rate up to 24 papers ('not willing', 'willing', or 'eager') to refine assignments. This data, together with conflicts and quotas, is used to assign papers.
